quick.topic: Ask what breaks at ten times
quick.summary: Why a pipeline that works today can fail next year, and the question that finds out.
quick.takeaway: Before building, ask what breaks at ten times the size.

parts.title: Ask what breaks at ten times

beats.line: My pipeline handled launch fine. Six months later it takes nine hours. What went wrong?
Nothing new. The data grew, and one step grew faster.
Usually the one that reads everything, every run.
Ask it early. At ten times the data, what breaks first?
Isn’t that building for a problem we don’t have?
You only ask the question. Then fix the one step that would break.
Here, process only the new day, not all of history.
At ten times, the full reread breaks. So I load each day once.
Now growth costs you minutes, not hours.

quiz.question: Which pipeline step is most likely to fail as data grows?
options: One that rereads all history on every run
One that processes only the newest day
One that sends a completion message
One that reads a small settings file
quiz.explanation: Work that scales with all history grows with the data, while daily work stays about the same.

quiz.question: Asking what breaks at ten times the data means building everything for ten times the data now.
quiz.explanation: It only finds the step that would break first, so you can design that one step sensibly.
